newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - March 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - March 5.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- CONFIDENT CHANCELLOR LIFTS MARKET

The stock market closed at a new high yesterday following the Chancellor Kenneth Clarke's upbeat assessment of economic prospects on Monday. The FT-SE index of leading shares rose 50.6 points to an all time high of 4357.7. Also, the pound performed well against the French franc and other European currencies, and climbed to its highest level against the German mark since September 1992 when it left the exchange rate mechanism.
-- LITTLEWOODS PUTS SALE SIGN ON STORES

Littlewoods, Britain's largest private retailer, is to sell its 135 high street stores and concentrate on its home shopping business. Littlewoods hope the sale of the stores will realise substantially more than 500 million pounds stg. Analysts suggest that Tesco, BHS and Marks & Spencer may be interested in picking the best stores, but none say anyone wanting the whole business. Littlewoods also announced pre-tax profits up by 15 percent to 112 million pounds stg last year.
-- MFI'S WINTER SALE FALLS FLAT AND KNOCKS SHARES 40 PENCE

MFI Furniture said yesterday that it's winter sale had been disappointing, then saw its share price tumble 40.5p to 156.5p. Chief executive John Randall said the market had changed against them, and had no explanation as to why the demand had fled.
THE TIMES
-- GENERAL ACCIDENT TO LIFT PAYOUT 10 PERCENT

General Accident is to increase its dividend by more than 10 percent despite a fall in full year profits to 421 million pounds stg. The company also said it had ruled out the acquisition of a UK life company and will instead concentrate on building up its mutual life insurer, Provident Mutual. Chief executive Bob Scott said he wants to build the group's life and pensions operations with the goal of increasing the proportion of life earnings to a level that covers dividends every year.
-- LADBROKE CLOSING PROPERTY DIVISION

Hotels and betting company Ladbroke is to shut its property division at a cost of 52 million pounds stg. Ladbroke completed the sale of 10 commercial and residential properties to Minerva yesterday for 25 million pounds stg and an office block in Boston to HN Gorin for US$23 million. The charge will be made to cover the cost of losses on disposals and a provision to write down the value of its remaining property assets.
-- THISTLE STALKS GROWTH

Britain's second largest hotel group, Thistle Hotels, is looking to add 2,000 rooms to its 13,250 rooms at 100 sites over the next few years as it concentrates on organic growth. The group announced a 73 percent increase in pre-tax profits, excluding exceptional items, to 60 million pounds stg. Analysts were disappointed with the results, which were not as strong as those of rival companies. Shares in Thistle fell 8p to 198p.
THE GUARDIAN
-- REINING IN GLOBAL MARKETS

The Chancellor Kenneth Clarke, speaking at a seminar in the City of London yesterday, said talks were in advanced stages for a tighter system of global financial regulations to deal with new products such as derivatives and with crisis across national boundaries. Britain is pushing for the designation of a lead regulator for each international financial group, with responsibility for pulling together regulation. Mr Clarke and finance ministers from other G7 countries are hoping that an improved regulation system will be in place by the summer.
-- 200 MILLION POUNDS ORDER FOR SOUTHEND LINE

Prism rail have made an order for 200 million pounds stg in nerw rolling stock on the heavily used commuter line between London and Southend. The order centres around a contract for 44 state-of-the-art trains to be built by Adtranz and supplied by Porterbrook, the train leading company who will maintain them.
-- SCRAMBLED PRICING PUTS BT ON LINE FOR MARKET DOMINATION

British Telecom has been allowed to keep its grip on the UK market due to constant and confusing price changes, and misplaced regulatory policy, according to a report yesterday by the National Utility Services. It says a legacy of misdirected pricing initiatives has left BT in a dominant position and able to control the market by igniting price wars and confusing consumers with constantly changing tariffs. The report also criticised the telecom regulator's continued use of price caps.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- BT STARTS TO WIN OVER US SHAREHOLDERS

British Telecom is to try to convince US investors of the benefits of its planned merger with the long distance carrier MCI with an unprecedented marketing campaign. At a series of roadshows for the US investment community in the coming weeks, BT hopes to convince shareholders not to sell stock immediately after the merger is completed. BT claim the merger will boost both sides' profits by 500 million pounds stg in five years through improved global marketing and savings on equipment.
-- HALIFAX COULD HAVE ANOTHER 3 BILLION POUNDS TO HAND OUT

Following its June flotation on the stock market, Halifax Building Society could have another 3 billion pounds stg to spend or return to shareholders. The calculations are based on Halifax's tier one capital ratio of 14 percent, well above the Bank of England's requirement that banks maintain a ratio of 4 percent, and most high street banks operating with ratios of 6-8 percent. The excess could be returned to shareholders, providing they remain investors, or fund acquisitions or development of existing businesses.
-- SUPPLIERS ASK WATCHDOG TO BLOCK BRITISH GAS PRICE CUTS

Independent gas suppliers and consumers have asked industry regulator to block new price cuts announced by British Gas GAS.L. British Gas Home Energy confirmed it is offering households in the southwest discounts of 12 percent to stop the loss of customers, but the Gas Consumers' Council said the price reductions were premature, and rival gas suppliers said that if British Gas was unchecked it could spoil government plans to liberalise the domestic market. Clare Spottiswoode, director of Ofgas, has launched a four-week consultation exercise before deciding whether the price cuts should be allowed to stand.
